hero.description: Boston hosts the 2026 tournament at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough — the legendary home of the New England Patriots and Revolution. Boston's fierce sports culture, massive immigrant soccer community, world-class universities, and historic heart guarantee an atmosphere built for the occasion. This is a city that takes sports seriously.

stadium.name: Gillette Stadium
stadium.transport: Gillette Stadium is in Foxborough, about 40 km south of Boston. On match days, MBTA Commuter Rail runs special game-day trains from South Station (about 55 min) — this is far and away the best option. Trains sell out for major events, so book in advance. Rideshare and driving are alternatives but traffic after matches is severe.

quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Fan hubs expected at City Hall Plaza and Faneuil Hall; confirm schedules

weather.june: Warm and pleasant, highs 22–26°C (72–79°F). Boston's best month for outdoor events — mild and occasionally rainy.
weather.july: Warm and sometimes humid, highs 26–30°C (79–86°F). Generally excellent conditions for fans.
packing_tips: A light rain layer — Boston weather can shift quickly
Sunscreen for outdoor fan zones and Faneuil Hall events
Layers for evening matches — temperatures cool after sunset
Comfortable shoes — Boston is a very walkable city

airports.name: Logan International Airport
airports.distance_to_stadium: About 55 km from Gillette Stadium; 5 km from Downtown Boston
transfer_options: Silver Line SL1 bus (free): Logan to South Station in 15–20 minutes
MBTA Blue Line: Airport station to downtown; transfer at Government Center for other lines
Rideshare from Logan to Downtown Boston takes 15–30 minutes depending on traffic
Water taxi from Logan to Long Wharf operates seasonally — a unique arrival experience
airports.notes: One of the most convenient US airports for a downtown hotel transfer. Silver Line is free from Logan to South Station. For Gillette Stadium, take the Silver Line or MBTA to South Station, then the match-day Commuter Rail to Foxborough.

public_transit: MBTA Commuter Rail match-day service: South Station to Foxborough/Patriot Place — about 55 minutes
Trains run before and after major events — book early as capacity is limited
Check mbta.com/events for game-day schedules close to each match date
rideshare: Rideshare from Downtown Boston to Gillette takes 45–60 min without traffic
Post-match rideshare surge from Foxborough is extreme — wait 45+ minutes or take the train back
Designated rideshare zones at Patriot Place adjacent to the stadium
driving_parking: Gillette Stadium has extensive parking — pre-book through the official lots online
Route 1 and I-95 back up severely after matches — plan a 90-minute buffer for departure
Patriot Place adjacent to the stadium has restaurants and shops to occupy time post-match while traffic clears
walking_biking: Not walkable from Boston — Foxborough is a suburban location
Patriot Place around the stadium is walkable for restaurants and pre-match activities
match_day_tips: Book Commuter Rail tickets before match day — they sell out for major events
Patriot Place restaurants and bars are great for post-match dining while waiting for traffic to clear
The stadium can be cold in the evening — bring a layer regardless of the forecast

fan_hubs.name: Boston Fan Hub — City Hall Plaza
fan_hubs.location: City Hall Plaza, 1 City Hall Square, Boston
fan_hubs.description: Boston's main civic plaza in Government Center is expected to host a major fan hub with giant screens, live entertainment, and food from the city's diverse communities. Central MBTA access from multiple lines.
transport_tips: MBTA Blue or Green Line to Government Center station
Walking distance from Faneuil Hall and the Financial District
MBTA Orange Line to Haymarket, short walk

fan_hubs.name: Faneuil Hall Fan Block
fan_hubs.location: Faneuil Hall Marketplace, 4 S Market St, Boston
fan_hubs.description: Boston's iconic marketplace district transforms into a fan hub on match days. Bars, restaurants, and outdoor space make Faneuil Hall one of the best pre-match atmospheres in the city. The Quincy Market Colonnade is spectacular on summer evenings.
transport_tips: MBTA Blue Line to Government Center or Aquarium
Walking distance from most downtown hotels
North Station (MBTA Green/Orange Lines) is a short walk away

neighborhoods.name: Seaport / South Boston Waterfront
neighborhoods.best_for: Modern hotels, South Station proximity, waterfront
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe, modern district. Well-lit and active throughout.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: South Station is walking distance — match-day Commuter Rail to Foxborough from there
neighborhoods.description: Boston's newest neighbourhood with modern hotels, the ICA, and excellent restaurants. Walking distance to South Station for the Gillette Commuter Rail. Omni Boston Seaport and Renaissance Waterfront are both excellent.

neighborhoods.name: Back Bay
neighborhoods.best_for: Classic Boston, Newbury St, walkable luxury
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Very safe and well-maintained. Boston's most upscale residential area.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: MBTA Orange Line to Back Bay, then to South Station for match-day train
neighborhoods.description: The classic Boston hotel district with Copley Square, Newbury Street boutiques, and Trinity Church. Excellent restaurants and walkable to most of Boston's best attractions.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown / Financial District
neighborhoods.best_for: Business hotels, South Station walk, fan hub proximity
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe and busy during the day. Quieter at night but well-lit.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Walk to South Station, then match-day Commuter Rail
neighborhoods.description: Convenient and central. Walking distance to South Station (Commuter Rail hub), Faneuil Hall, and multiple T lines. Good value compared to Back Bay.

neighborhoods.name: Cambridge
neighborhoods.best_for: University atmosphere, intellectual culture, Harvard and MIT
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Very safe. Active student and academic neighbourhood.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: MBTA Red Line to South Station, then match-day Commuter Rail — about 30–40 min
neighborhoods.description: Just across the river from Boston — Harvard Square, MIT, and a vibrant café scene. A unique base with a different energy from Downtown Boston.

hotels.name: Omni Boston Hotel at the Seaport
hotels.distance: South Station (Commuter Rail hub) is walkable
hotels.best_for: Luxury, waterfront views, South Station proximity

hotels.name: Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel
hotels.best_for: Waterfront, business amenities, Commuter Rail access

hotels.name: Courtyard Foxborough Patriot Place
hotels.best_for: Stadium proximity, families, avoiding the commute

hotels.name: Fairmont Copley Plaza
hotels.distance: 25 min to South Station by walk/T
hotels.best_for: Classic Boston luxury, Copley Square, Newbury St

bars.name: The Banshee
bars.notes: Boston's best Irish pub for soccer — passionate, knowledgeable crowd and a packed atmosphere for major matches.
bars.transit: MBTA Red Line to Andrew, short walk

bars.name: Hennessy's
bars.notes: Traditional Irish bar right by Faneuil Hall — great match atmosphere and easy access from multiple T lines.
bars.transit: MBTA Blue Line to Aquarium or Government Center

bars.name: Who's On First
bars.notes: Fenway neighbourhood sports bar — draws a passionate sports crowd on major match days.

bars.name: The Harp
bars.notes: Long-running Irish sports bar near North Station. Reliable atmosphere for all major international matches.
bars.transit: MBTA Green/Orange Line to North Station

bars.name: Jerry Remy's Sports Bar
bars.notes: Popular Fenway-adjacent sports bar with multiple screens and an active crowd for World Cup.

transport.summary: Boston has the MBTA ("the T") — the oldest US transit system. For Gillette Stadium, match-day Commuter Rail from South Station is the essential option. For Boston itself, the T covers the city efficiently.
tips: MBTA Commuter Rail match-day service from South Station to Foxborough: book early, trains sell out
CharlieCard is the contactless payment for the T — buy at any MBTA station
Logan Airport connects to Downtown via free Silver Line SL1 to South Station
Amtrak from South Station connects to New York (3.5 hrs) and Washington DC (7 hrs) via high-speed Acela

fan_zones.name: Boston Fan Hub — City Hall Plaza
fan_zones.location: City Hall Plaza, 1 City Hall Square, Boston
fan_zones.description: Boston's main civic plaza expected to host a tournament fan hub with giant screens and live entertainment.

fan_zones.name: Faneuil Hall Fan Block
fan_zones.location: Faneuil Hall Marketplace, 4 S Market St
fan_zones.description: Iconic marketplace district that becomes a natural fan zone with outdoor bars, screens, and summer evening energy.

soccer_culture.community_notes: Boston has deep soccer roots through its large Irish, Portuguese, Brazilian, Haitian, and Latin American communities. New England Revolution has passionate supporters, and the region's universities add a young international fan base. This is not a casual soccer city.

tourist_hits.name: Freedom Trail
tourist_hits.notes: 3-km walk through 16 Revolutionary War sites — from Boston Common to Bunker Hill. Free to walk independently.

tourist_hits.name: Fenway Park
tourist_hits.notes: America's oldest baseball park — tour it even if the Red Sox aren't playing.

tourist_hits.name: Harvard University
tourist_hits.notes: Beautiful historic campus — walk through Harvard Yard and visit the natural history museums.

tourist_hits.name: Museum of Fine Arts
tourist_hits.notes: One of the USA's great art museums. Wednesday evenings are free after 4pm.

local_favorites.name: North End
local_favorites.notes: Boston's Italian neighbourhood — the best cannoli in the USA at Mike's Pastry or Modern Pastry. Heated debate. Try both.

local_favorites.name: Institute of Contemporary Art
local_favorites.notes: Stunning harbour-facing building with excellent rotating exhibitions.

local_favorites.name: Arnold Arboretum
local_favorites.notes: 247-acre Harvard-affiliated garden — perfect for a morning run or quiet afternoon between matches.

areas: North End (Hanover St) — Italian restaurants and pastry shops
Back Bay / Newbury St — upscale dining and cocktail bars
Seaport — modern restaurants and waterfront dining
Cambridge — Harvard Square restaurants and independent bars

recommendations.name: Legal Sea Foods
recommendations.notes: The iconic Boston seafood chain — clam chowder is mandatory. Multiple locations.

recommendations.name: Menton
recommendations.notes: Barbara Lynch's fine dining flagship in Fort Point. Book well ahead.

recommendations.name: Toro
recommendations.notes: Spanish-inspired tapas in the South End — one of Boston's most celebrated restaurants.

local_resources.emergency_info: Emergency: 911. Non-emergency Boston Police: (617) 343-4633. Hospital: Massachusetts General Hospital, (617) 726-2000.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Downtown Boston, Back Bay, the North End, and Beacon Hill are exceptionally walkable — compact and mostly flat. The Harborwalk and Charles River Esplanade are scenic walking routes.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: Bluebikes (bikeshare) operates throughout Boston and Cambridge. The Charles River path is ideal for cycling.
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: Bluebikes has docks throughout Boston, Cambridge, and Somerville. Day passes available at any dock station or in the Bluebikes app.

pickup_soccer.name: Fens (Back Bay Fens)
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Informal pickup games on weekends near the community garden area of the Fens park.

pickup_soccer.name: Magazine Beach, Cambridge
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Fields along the Charles River with active community soccer, especially from the Brazilian community.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Cape Cod
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Classic New England summer escape. Sandy beaches, seafood shacks, and a relaxed pace. Good between matches — take the bus from South Station.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Acadia National Park
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Stunning Maine coastline and granite peaks. Best as a weekend trip between Boston matches — drive or take bus to Bar Harbor.

safety_tips: Boston is a very safe city for tourists — Downtown, Back Bay, Seaport, and Cambridge are all low-risk
Use the MBTA for late-night travel rather than walking in unfamiliar areas after midnight
Gillette Stadium crowds on match days are large — keep close to your group near exits
Book Commuter Rail tickets for Foxborough in advance — capacity is limited for popular matches
Boston drivers can be aggressive — cross streets carefully and follow pedestrian signals
